byHand.title: By hand
byHand.teaser: You read your meters and enter the readings, in a browser or on your phone.
byHand.forWhom: For anyone who reads their own meters and needs no further technology at home.
byHand.get1: Consumption and costs per utility, compared with the previous year.
byHand.get2: **The balance:** will you pay more, or get something back?
byHand.get3: Forecast, deadlines and notes on your contracts.
byHand.get4: Bill checks and the annual report.
byHand.software: The Energietracker, most easily as a Docker container, otherwise on a NAS or web server with PHP 8.3 or later. Plus an up-to-date browser.
byHand.hardware: **A computer or NAS on your home network.** A phone is enough for entering readings.
byHand.effort: **Set it up once:** the “First steps” guide allows about 15 minutes. After that you only enter readings, as often as you like. Two readings give the first consumption figure.
byHand.step2: **Go through the setup:** language and country, who you are, which energy sources you use.
byHand.step4: Add your contract so that costs and balance are right.
byHand.step5: **Set your location:** the app needs the weather for heating degree days and the forecast.
byHand.step6: Add your phone if you want to enter readings at the meter.
byHand.data: **Everything is stored as files on your server, with no account and no telemetry.** Only the weather sync goes out: your location, rounded to about 1 km, to Open-Meteo. You can switch it off under {connections} → {weather}. The place search only asks there when you use it.
byHand.limit1: **Between two readings the app spreads consumption evenly over the days.** It does not measure, and it says which figure is spread.
byHand.limit2: **No quarter-hours:** assessing flexibility and storage takes values per quarter-hour.
byHand.limit3: **Nothing arrives by itself:** without a new entry the figures stay as they were.
byHand.detailIntro: **Docker packs the Energietracker with everything it needs into a container.** Your data stays outside it, in the folder you mount.

docker.label: Docker
docker.note: Port 8080 on the computer leads to port 80 in the container.

web.label: Apache, nginx, Synology Web Station
web.note: **Under the folder where you put the app.** Apache uses the included `.htaccess`.

byHand.note1: **Everything is in `/data` in the container, here in the `data` folder next to the command.** You can also back up in the app: {settings} → {data}.
byHand.note2: The image is available for amd64 and arm64, so also for computers with an ARM processor.
byHand.note3: **Without sign-in, anyone who can reach the address can read and change everything.** Switch sign-in on under {settings} → {access}.
byHand.note4: **Opening it as an app on the home screen and without a network takes HTTPS.** In a browser on your home network it works without.

err1.fix: Choose another port on the computer, such as `-p 9000:80`.

err2.fix: **No folder was mounted.** Always start with `-v`, using a folder or a named volume.

err3.fix: **The folder is not shared.** Share it under `Settings → Resources → File sharing` or use `-v energietracker-data:/data`.

err4.fix: The data folder does not belong to the container’s UID: `sudo chown -R 10001:0 ./data` or a named volume.

localAi.title: With local AI
localAi.teaser: You ask in your own words. Model and figures stay at home.
localAi.forWhom: For anyone who wants to ask about their figures in their own words, without questions or figures leaving the house. You should not mind Docker, or have someone who helps with the setup.
localAi.get1: Answers to questions like “What is my gas balance?”, with the same figures as in the app.
localAi.get2: **The source of every figure:** measured, entered, spread, assumed or estimated.
localAi.get3: Ready-made tasks for the monthly report, annual report, bill check and deadlines.
localAi.get4: **Proposals instead of changes:** the AI enters nothing itself, you confirm in the app.
localAi.software: Energietracker from v3.12.0, Docker with Open WebUI 0.6.31 or later in it, plus Ollama with a model that can use tools. Exactly this combination has been tested: Open WebUI with local Ollama. Other local programs are experimental.
localAi.hardware: A computer with plenty of memory, ideally with a GPU the model can use. The smaller the computer, the longer an answer takes. The Energietracker may run on another device on your home network.
localAi.effort: **More than one installation:** three programs, a large download for the model and a connection you enter. After that you just ask. How long an answer takes depends on model and computer; the guide gives measured values.
localAi.step1: The Energietracker runs on your home network.
localAi.step2: **Install Ollama and get a model that can use tools.** The guide shows the installation with an image model; here, take a language model with the `tools` capability.
localAi.step3: Start Open WebUI in a container.
localAi.step4: Under {connections}, open the “{card}” card, choose “{sw}” and create a “{read}” key.
localAi.step5: In Open WebUI, as an administrator, add the Energietracker as a tool server: type MCP (Streamable HTTP), address and key.
localAi.step6: Switch the tool on in the chat and ask.
localAi.data: **Question, figures and answer stay on your home network: Ollama runs on your computer.** That holds as long as you add no cloud model and no web search in Open WebUI. Only the programs and the model come from the internet, once. The AI gets identifiers and originals only with the switches “{ids}” and “{originals}”; both are off by default. The weather sync is the same for every way.
localAi.limit1: **The AI does not calculate, it tells.** It can get things wrong while doing so. Check important figures in the app.
localAi.limit2: **No tools for settings, people, keys, backups or deleting.** That stays in the app.
localAi.limit3: Long extractions with a local model and reports as PDF stay in the app.
localAi.limit4: Programs that only speak SSE or insist on OAuth do not connect.
localAi.limit5: The public demo has no AI interface, because it runs without a server.
localAi.detailIntro: **The usual setup:** Open WebUI in a container, Ollama natively on the computer, the Energietracker on the same computer or the NAS. Open WebUI is the hub: it sends your question to Ollama and calls the Energietracker’s tools itself. The model never talks to the Energietracker directly.

browser.label: Browser → Open WebUI
browser.note: Port 3000 on the computer leads to port 8080 in the container.

ollama.label: Open WebUI → Ollama
ollama.note: **Inside the container, `localhost` is the container itself.** Unless told otherwise, Open WebUI looks for Ollama at this address.

sameHost.label: Open WebUI → Energietracker on the same computer
sameHost.note: **This is the address you enter in Open WebUI.** It only accepts `POST` with a key, so testing in a browser does not help.

otherHost.label: Open WebUI → Energietracker on another device with Docker
otherHost.note: With that device’s address on your home network.

apache.label: Open WebUI → Energietracker on Apache or Synology Web Station
apache.note: **Here `api.php` belongs in the address.** The “{card}” card always shows the address with `api.php`; it works with every web server.

localAi.codeTitle: Template based on the manufacturers’ guides
localAi.note1: On a Mac, Ollama runs as its own program next to Docker, not in a container: Docker Desktop does not pass the GPU through. That is what Ollama says. On Linux with an Nvidia card, the `ollama/ollama` container works too.
localAi.note2: **`host.docker.internal` points to the computer under Docker Desktop (Mac, Windows).** On Linux the name only exists with `extra_hosts`, as in the file above.
localAi.note3: **Keys:** “{read}” may use all reading tools, prompts and resources. “{write}” may also read documents and propose changes. Start with “{read}”. The app shows the key (`etk_…`) only once; other keys do not work here.
localAi.note4: **“{applyInApp}” is on by default: even if the AI wants to apply a change, it writes nothing.** You confirm the proposal under “{proposals}”.
localAi.note5: **The interface is off by default.** `ET_MCP=off` locks it firmly, even if someone flips the switch.

err1.fix: **No key, or a wrong one.** Create revoked keys again.

err2.fix: The “{sw}” switch is off, or `ET_MCP=off` is set.

err3.fix: The key has no AI scope, or a proposing tool was called with “{read}”.

err4.fix: **Wrong address.** On Apache and Synology, `api.php` belongs in it.

err5.fix: You have set a host list (`ET_ALLOWED_HOSTS` or under {settings} → {access}), and `host.docker.internal` is not on it.

err6.fix: **Is Ollama running?** If the container cannot get through, set `OLLAMA_HOST=0.0.0.0` (on a Mac with `launchctl setenv`) and restart Ollama. Ollama has no sign-in: do not expose the port to the internet.

err7.fix: **Reload the page and switch the tool on in the chat.** The model must have the `tools` capability.

inbox.title: With supplier mail
inbox.teaser: PDF into the inbox. You check what was read and take it over.
inbox.forWhom: For anyone who has bills and contract letters as PDFs and does not want to type them in. Works without AI too: the inbox is then the place to file your mail.
inbox.get1: Contracts, bills, meters and readings from the document, every field with its literal source passage and page.
inbox.get2: **One sentence for each document:** what the letter means for you and what to do now.
inbox.get3: A file on every contract and meter with all its documents.
inbox.get4: On a price change, a note on your rights.
inbox.software: **The Energietracker is enough for filing.** To read documents, your own service on your home network (Ollama or OpenAI-compatible such as LM Studio) or a cloud service (experimental).
inbox.hardware: **For local reading, a computer on which a language model runs smoothly.** Filing works from any device.
inbox.effort: **Filing works right away.** To read documents you install a service, load a model and enter the address, or choose a provider and key in the cloud. You check every document yourself, and locally it takes a while; the guide says how long.
inbox.step1: Put the first PDF into the inbox.
inbox.step2: **If it should be read:** set up local or cloud under {connections} → {reading}.
inbox.step3: Check the proposal next to the document and take it over.
inbox.step4: Bring in mail in other ways too, if you like.
inbox.data: **The PDF stays on your server and travels with every backup.** Locally, only the text goes to your service on your home network. In the cloud, every document you send for reading goes to the chosen service, including name, address and numbers; the app asks first and sends nothing without your consent. No other data of your household leaves. The weather sync is the same for every way.
inbox.limit1: **The inbox does not read photos and scans without a text layer.** You enter those by hand.
inbox.limit2: PDF only, up to 10 MB per file.
inbox.limit3: **Without a service set up, nothing reads along.** You then file, assign and enter by hand.
inbox.limit4: **The AI only proposes.** What you confirm is taken over.
inbox.detailIntro: **The browser reads the PDF’s text layer and sends it to your server.** The server sends it, without the pages of terms and conditions, to your service. Its address must be on your own network; the app checks this on every call.

ollama.label: Local with Ollama
ollama.note: From inside a container, Ollama must listen on the network: `OLLAMA_HOST=0.0.0.0`.

lmstudio.label: Local, OpenAI-compatible (such as LM Studio)
lmstudio.note: The address goes up to and including `/v1`.

api.label: Filing a PDF from outside the app
api.note: With a key; shortcuts and email via Home Assistant use the same entrance.

inbox.note1: The watched folder is called `posteingang/` and lives in the data directory.
inbox.note2: **Only people who manage the installation may set up reading.** The card has its own save button.
inbox.note3: **All cloud routes are experimental:** they have not yet been tested with real feedback.

err1.symptom: “No service is set up for reading”
err1.fix: Enter the address under {connections} → {reading} and test the connection.

err2.symptom: The document has no text layer
err2.fix: **It is a scan.** Enter it by hand; the PDF stays as a record.

err3.symptom: No answer within the time limit
err3.fix: **The first read after a pause loads the model into memory first.** Try again.

homeAssistant.title: With Home Assistant
homeAssistant.teaser: Home Assistant delivers the readings, the Energietracker calculates and reports back.
homeAssistant.forWhom: For anyone already using Home Assistant or wanting to read smart meters. The Energietracker reads no meters itself; Home Assistant does that.
homeAssistant.get1: Readings arrive by themselves, daily or every 15 minutes.
homeAssistant.get2: With values per quarter-hour, also the analyses of flexibility and storage.
homeAssistant.get3: **Back in Home Assistant:** sensors for balance, consumption, forecast and “To do”, without YAML through the HACS integration.
homeAssistant.get4: Notifications about deadlines and new documents, plus dates as a calendar.
homeAssistant.get5: With evcc, the wallbox’s charging sessions including the solar share.
homeAssistant.software: **Home Assistant.** The Energietracker as an app in Home Assistant OS (experimental) or as its own container. For the sensors, the HACS integration, from Home Assistant 2026.3.
homeAssistant.hardware: **What Home Assistant needs anyway, plus your smart meters or readers.** As an app, the Energietracker needs no device of its own.
homeAssistant.effort: **Create a token, give meters an alias, add a REST command and an automation.** That is YAML; anyone who knows Home Assistant will find their way quickly. The way back through the integration needs no YAML.
homeAssistant.step1: **Start the Energietracker:** as an app in Home Assistant OS or as its own container.
homeAssistant.step2: Under {connections} → {homeAssistant}, create the token and give the meters an alias.
homeAssistant.step3: Add the REST command and the automation in Home Assistant.
homeAssistant.step4: Install the HACS integration for the sensors.
homeAssistant.data: **Everything stays on your home network:** Home Assistant and the Energietracker talk directly. The app only sends notifications once someone who manages the installation switches them on, and only to your Home Assistant. The weather sync is the same for every way.
homeAssistant.limit1: The Energietracker controls nothing. evcc or Home Assistant control the wallbox and storage; it does the sums.
homeAssistant.limit2: **The unit must match:** what Home Assistant delivers must fit the meter’s unit, or the readings will be wrong.
homeAssistant.limit3: Heating oil and pellets work with deliveries and do not go through this entrance.
homeAssistant.detailIntro: **Home Assistant sends the readings with `POST /api/ingest` and a token (`et_…`).** On the way back it reads `/api/summary` and `/api/todo`; with sign-in on, that takes a read key, the token does not apply there.

ingest.label: Home Assistant → Energietracker
ingest.note: With `api.php` it always works; with a rewrite rule in the web server, also without.

summary.label: Energietracker → sensors
summary.note: The integration asks every 15 minutes and creates the sensors itself.

app.label: App in Home Assistant, from outside it
app.note: **The sidebar runs through Ingress.** For other programs, open a port in the app under Configuration → Network, such as `8095`.

homeAssistant.note1: **`!secret` only works as a whole value.** So `secrets.yaml` holds `"Bearer et_…"` including `Bearer`.
homeAssistant.note2: Home Assistant’s “Model Context Protocol” integration does not work: it only speaks SSE.
homeAssistant.note3: Anything that can send an HTTP request delivers through the same entrance, including ioBroker, Node-RED and openHAB.

err1.fix: **Wrong token or missing header.** Use `Authorization: !secret energietracker_auth` as a whole value.

err2.fix: **The alias does not match the meter.** Check it in the settings.

err3.symptom: The value arrives but does not count
err3.fix: **It is lower than the previous reading and therefore flagged as suspect.** Check it in the utility’s view.

cloudAi.title: With cloud AI (experimental)
cloudAi.teaser: The model runs at the provider. What it reads leaves your home.
cloudAi.forWhom: For anyone without a computer for a local model who deliberately decides that figures may leave the house.
cloudAi.get1: The same figures with their source as on the local way.
cloudAi.get2: No computer of your own for the model.
cloudAi.get3: “{applyInApp}” stays on: the AI cannot change anything without you.
cloudAi.software: Energietracker from v3.12.0, an AI program with MCP over HTTP that can send a key, and an account with the model provider. All these routes are experimental: they follow the manufacturers’ guides and we have not tested them.
cloudAi.hardware: An ordinary computer is enough; the model runs at the provider.
cloudAi.effort: **Set up one program and enter the key.** On top come costs with the provider, at its prices.
cloudAi.step1: The Energietracker runs on your home network.
cloudAi.step2: Choose a program that runs on your computer and speaks MCP over HTTP.
cloudAi.step3: Under {connections}, open the “{card}” card, choose “{sw}” and create a “{read}” key.
cloudAi.step4: Connect the program as the guide shows for yours.
cloudAi.step5: Read what goes out and check the provider’s terms.
cloudAi.data: What the AI reads, the model provider sees: your questions and the tools’ answers, meaning figures on consumption, costs and contracts. Passwords and keys, settings with network addresses, the list of people, backups and logs never leave. Identifiers and originals only with the switches “{ids}” and “{originals}”; both are off by default. The weather sync is the same for every way.
cloudAi.limit1: **Programs that connect from their provider’s cloud cannot reach your home network.** That only works by following the guide, with your own HTTPS access, and it puts an entry point on the internet.
cloudAi.limit2: **No OAuth:** programs that insist on OAuth sign-in do not connect.
cloudAi.limit3: **No tools for settings, people, keys, backups or deleting.** That stays in the app.
cloudAi.limit4: **Experimental means:** feedback is welcome, and things may change.
cloudAi.detailIntro: Examples of such programs, all experimental: Claude Code, VS Code (Copilot Chat) and Cursor on your computer. The program talks to the Energietracker on your home network and sends what it reads to its model.

program.label: AI program on your computer → Energietracker
program.note: On Apache and Synology, `api.php` belongs in the address.

public.label: Service from the cloud → your own HTTPS access
public.note: **Only if the service allows its own header with the key.** The reverse proxy lets only `/api/mcp` through. This is a guide, not a recommendation.

cloudAi.note1: **Create a separate key for each program and device.** Start with “{read}”; “{write}” may also propose.
cloudAi.note2: A cloud model in Open WebUI is also experimental: the data then goes to the provider.
cloudAi.note3: **Revoke the key as soon as you no longer need the access.** Rate limits and the lockout after wrong keys apply here too.

err1.fix: **No key, or a wrong one.** Some programs then look for an OAuth sign-in and report an error about it; the cause is still the key.

err2.fix: The “{sw}” switch is off, or `ET_MCP=off` is set.

err3.fix: **Wrong address.** On Apache and Synology, `api.php` belongs in it.

together.title: All together
together.teaser: The building blocks complement each other, and none depends on another.
together.forWhom: For anyone who wants to combine several ways. You need not set everything up at once; each block runs on its own, and the order does not matter.
together.get1: Home Assistant delivers the readings; the mail delivers contracts and bills.
together.get2: The app checks the bill from the mail against your readings.
together.get3: The AI asks for everything in one place and gives the source of every figure.
together.get4: By hand always remains possible, for instance for the meter without a sensor.
together.software: What the individual ways need, nothing more.
together.hardware: **One computer can carry a lot:** Open WebUI in a container, Ollama natively, the Energietracker on the same computer or the NAS.
together.effort: The sum of the blocks, but step by step: you start with one and add the next when you need it.
together.step3: Put the mail into the inbox.
together.step4: Connect an AI, local or in the cloud.
together.data: **What you do not explicitly send out stays inside.** Only three things can leave: the weather sync (rounded location, can be switched off), documents to a cloud service (after asking) and what a cloud AI reads (only if you connect one).
together.limit1: More blocks mean more programs to keep up to date.
together.limit2: The Energietracker controls nothing, not even together with the others.
together.limit3: **An AI does not replace checking:** you confirm what it proposes, and you look up important figures in the app.
together.detailIntro: **Every block has its address.** Replace the placeholders with yours.
